title: Nvidia's Medical Fine-Tuning Cuts Nemotron 3.5 Transcription Error Rate by 45.8%
summary:
The chipmaker released a technical case study demonstrating how adapting its latest speech-to-text model to specialized data can reduce mistakes in transcription. Domain-specific fine-tuning of Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe lowered the word error rate on medical recordings to 12.17% from a baseline of 22.44%, a performance gain achieved using about 14 GPU hours on a single GB300 processor. Nvidia is publishing the fine-tuning recipe alongside the model weights to provide developers a framework for tailoring the tool to specialized vocabularies.

Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is a 30B parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with roughly 4B active parameters that can process audio in 40 languages and identify separate speakers in the same recording. Designed for non-streaming audio up to one hour, the open-weight tool currently ranks first among open-weight models on the Hugging Face Open ASR English leaderboard. It is available for commercial use under the OpenMDW-1.1 license.

selectedTweets.text:
NVIDIA’s Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe includes an interesting medical transcription case study.

Using the best prompt, the model had a 22.44% word error rate. After domain-specific fine-tuning, that fell to 12.17% on recordings from held-out speakers—a 45.8% relative reduction.

The adaptation took about 14 GPU-hours on one GB300. NVIDIA is publishing the recipe alongside the open-weight model, giving developers a concrete example of adapting speech recognition to specialized vocabulary.

selectedTweets.text:
NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe ties for #1 among open weights Speech to Text models with 2.8% WER, using just 4B active parameters

Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is NVIDIA's new open weights Speech to Text model for non-streaming transcription, with 30B total and 4B active parameters, and the most accurate NVIDIA model on our non-streaming Speech to Text leaderboard.

Key takeaways

➤ Accuracy: Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe scores 2.8% on the AA-WER Index, tied with Mistral's Voxtral Small for #1 among open-weight models. It leads Voxtral Small on AA-AgentTalk, our dataset of voice agent conversations, at 1.8% vs. 2.3%.

➤ Model size: With 4B active parameters (30B total), Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe sits on the open weights frontier of AA-WER vs. active parameters. It matches the accuracy of Mistral's Voxtral Small with 6x fewer active parameters (4B vs. 24B), while other open weights models of a similar size sit at around 4% WER.

Congratulations to @NVIDIAAI on the release!

See more details below ⬇️
